title: fractalwright: name, visibility, scope, AI styling, browser accelerator

questions.title: Final name
questions.question: What should the plugin be called?
questions.background: The working name is fractalwright, matching the other -wright plugins (pixelwright, polywright, musicwright). Design note: D:/m4bwa/Claude/Projects/Ai/fractalwright/ai-docs/plans/design.md.
questions.why: The name goes into the repo, the plugin manifest and every skill name; renaming later costs a migration.

guess.why: Plain, searchable, and fits the -wright family.

questions.title: Repository visibility
questions.question: When should the fractalwright repository be public?
questions.background: Most of your plugins go public (pixelwright, polywright); some start private until evals pass (lexwright). Making a repo public is a repository-settings change, so it waits on you.
questions.why: Decides whether the repo is created private now and when the switch happens.

options.label: Private until v0.1 passes its evals, then public (switch waits on you)

guess.why: Matches how lexwright was handled and keeps an untested plugin out of view.

questions.title: Neighbours in v1 scope
questions.question: Which neighbouring pattern families belong in fractalwright v1?
questions.background: Fractals border other generative pattern families. Each added family costs shaders, presets and evals. Ones left out can come later.
questions.why: Sets the v1 scope and the size of the plugin.

guess.why: Reaction-diffusion is one shader and looks fractal-like; CA and tilings are their own fields (out); Kleinian sets fit but are heavier, so later rather than v1.

questions.title: AI styling
questions.question: How should AI styling (img2img or video restyle over the math render) work in v1?
questions.background: The core renders exact math. An AI pass through ComfyUI could restyle frames, but then the result is no longer the exact fractal.
questions.why: Decides whether v1 ships a ComfyUI styling step and its default.

options.label: Optional, off by default, outputs marked "interpreted"

guess.why: Keeps exact renders the default while allowing the look when asked, clearly labelled.

questions.title: Headless browser accelerator
questions.question: Should Playwright driving headless system Edge be the first optional accelerator?
questions.background: Measured 1080p Mandelbrot frame: NumPy 6 s, Playwright + system Edge WebGL2 0.2 s. Install is 118 MB pip (Playwright incl. its Node driver); no Chromium download since Edge ships with Windows. One shader serves stills, video, the interactive page and 3D. moderngl is faster (0.03 s float64) at ~1 MB but serves only Python outputs. Details in design.md section 1.
questions.why: Decides which optional dependency v1 builds around first.

options.label: Yes: Playwright + system Edge first (118 MB)
No accelerator in v1, NumPy only

guess.why: 30x faster than NumPy and the only route where one shader serves all five outputs.
